Harry Brook’s 202 makes him England’s first ODI double‑centurion and sets new fastest‑double‑century record

29 Oct 2026, 02:22 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.indiatoday.in

3 min read

Match summary

On 22 October 2026, England faced Sri Lanka in the third match of the ODI tri‑series at Rawalpindi, Pakistan. England posted a massive 429 for 4 in 50 overs, the highest ODI total ever recorded on Pakistani soil. Harry Brook, batting at No. 4 after Ben Duckett’s dismissal, anchored the innings with an unbeaten 202 off 116 balls. He was dismissed on the final ball of England’s innings, caught at short third, after having taken the side to a commanding total.

Record‑breaking milestones

  • Fastest double century in ODIs – Brook reached 200 in 114 deliveries, surpassing Shubman Gill’s previous record of 117 balls set against the West Indies in Guwahati last month.
  • England’s first men’s ODI double‑centurion – No English batsman had previously crossed the 200‑run mark in a One‑Day International.
  • Highest individual ODI score for England – Brook’s 202 eclipsed Ben Stokes’s 182* against New Zealand in 2023.
  • Triple‑century club – With this innings Brook joins Chris Gayle as the only player to have a triple hundred in Tests, a double hundred in ODIs, and a hundred in T20Is.
  • Joe Root milestone – Root’s 69 off 65 balls made him the first England player to accumulate 8,000 ODI runs.

Context and comparisons

Shubman Gill’s 223 off 133 balls, made in Guwahati, had been the benchmark for the fastest double century until Brook’s 114‑ball effort. Brook’s strike‑rate of 174.14 (202 runs off 116 balls) dwarfs many previous double‑century innings, while his boundary count – 21 fours and 10 sixes – reflects a blend of power and timing.

England’s total of 429/4 also set a new record for the highest ODI score in Pakistan, surpassing the previous best (which stood at 418/6 by South Africa in 2022). The run‑rate of 8.58 runs per over over the full 50 overs underscores the aggressive intent of the side.

Implications for England and the tri‑series

  • Batting depth – Brook’s ability to convert a modest start (13 off 24) into a 202‑run blitz demonstrates England’s depth beyond the top order. The late surge from Will Jacks (66 off 24) further highlights the bench strength.
  • Series momentum – A 429‑run total places Sri Lanka under immense pressure in the chase, giving England a substantial advantage in the tri‑series standings.
  • Captaincy credentials – All four of Brook’s ODI centuries have come since he assumed the England captaincy, suggesting a positive correlation between his leadership role and personal form.
  • Strategic considerations for opponents – Teams facing England will need to reassess bowling plans, especially in the middle overs where Brook accelerated 189 runs off 92 balls after a cautious start.

What remains uncertain

  • Sri Lanka’s response – The source does not provide Sri Lanka’s final total or whether they managed a successful chase, leaving the outcome of the match and its impact on the series table incomplete.
  • Injury or fatigue concerns – No information is given about Brook’s physical condition after such a demanding innings, which could affect his availability for upcoming fixtures.
  • Long‑term statistical impact – While the records set are clear, how this performance will influence future ODI strategies or player rankings remains to be seen.
